correctness.rationale: For compact invariant mu in the strictly positive quadrant and Q=xy^gamma, use arbitrary C1 one-coordinate antiderivatives F(x),G(y). Stationarity E[L F]=E[F_x(x)(1-Q)]=0 and E[L G]=alpha E[G_y(y)(Q-y)]=0 for all continuous tests gives conditional E[Q|x]=1 and E[Q|y]=y. Since x,y>0 derive E[y^gamma|x]=1/x and E[x|y]=y^(1-gamma), mean EQ=Ey=1, Cov(x,Q)=0, Cov(y,Q)=Var(y). The identity Q=1-xdot=y+ydot/alpha and E[ydot|y]=0 give E[xdot^2]=Var(Q)=Var(y)+alpha^-2 E[ydot^2]. If either speed-energy vanishes, invariant compact complete trajectories with a frozen x or y satisfy scalar linear equations and only equilibrium (1,1) remains. Strict Jensen on convex y^(1-gamma) and y^gamma yields E[x]>1 and E[1/x]>1 for every nonequilibrium compact stationary measure. These opposing moment inequalities force positive mass on x<1 and x>1, while Ey=1 and nonconstant y force both y sides. Strict activity terms yield 0<Corr(y,Q)<1 and its exact formula. For any nonconstant periodic orbit its invariant time measure crosses each level at least twice by continuity. Independent exact rational checks confirmed the two flux-speed algebraic identities; statistical conditional/equality cases are analytic, not inferred from the finite checker.
